deviations.what: chevalleySerre over the whole list runs on the main thread only up to 27 positions (RELATIONS_MAIN_MAX = CAPS.matrixGridDim). Above that it runs in the worker, called with a hint that has no expectedItems. A configured or default state still computes its list on the main thread at any size. So E7 node 7, after a pick, has its relation list computed in the worker.
deviations.why: The first chevalleySerre call for E7 node 7 in Chromium takes 14 ms at full speed, about 56 ms at 4x, which is over the 50 ms budget. B8 node 5 takes about 405 ms.

deviations.what: Residual on the largest orbits built (B8, C8, D8 nodes with 1120 and 1792 positions). At full speed, reading the worker's reply (57120 entries for B8 node 5, deserialized in lib/worker.ts) gave one task of 54 to 61 ms in about half the runs. At 4x, minusculeMatrices on 1792 positions (25 to 33 ms at full speed) plus that reply produced tasks of 100 to 270 ms.
deviations.why: minusculeMatrices stays on the main thread as E-9 rule 1 says. The reply size is fixed by chevalleySerre's return shape. See requests.

deviations.what: Formulas use a small MathML component of T12's own (RelationFormula.svelte, msub/msup/mrow) with the LinearForm RENDER fallback, not LinearForm itself
deviations.why: LinearForm has no commutator or power form

deviations.what: The orbit is drawn up to 300 positions and given as layer counts above. List tables and the orbit table are capped at 300 rows, with a sentence pointing to Download data. String lines list 12 positions (first six and last six); above 2000 positions, or with entries beyond 2^53, only the two ends are shown.
deviations.why: The specification gives no bound; T2's 300 was borrowed, and stringThrough takes safe numbers only

deviations.what: The panel order and the matrix node k are not in the state or the link
